title: Thirsty Singhs Are Provoked at Morinda

blocks.text: The page begins with hesitation at the top: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia wished to put it off because Abdali's forces might still be close, yet the poem insists that what is fated has to happen. The march therefore continues under a sense that providence is driving the encounter forward whether the chiefs want it or not.

That inevitability turns concrete when thirsty Singhs went to Morinda for water instead of pressing on in silence. From the town, armed Ranghars stand on the rooftops, watch the Sikhs below, and begin a campaign of provocation rather than letting the travelers pass.

What might have remained a delayed quarrel is thus made immediate by insult, posture, and the refusal of Morinda's men to keep peace. The page sets up the clash as a confrontation invited by the town itself.
